info.name: Order & Payment API
info.description:
Extendable order and payment management API (Laravel 13, JWT).

**Getting started**
1. Set `base_url` (collection variable) to your server, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1`.
2. Run **Authentication > Login** (demo account `demo@example.com` / `password`, after `php artisan db:seed`) or **Register**. The token is saved to `token` automatically and sent as a Bearer token by every other request.
3. **Create order** saves `order_id`; **Process payment** saves `payment_id`.

**Conventions**
- All responses are JSON. Successful bodies are wrapped in `data`; list endpoints add `links` and `meta` (pagination).
- Validation errors: **422** with `message` and an `errors` object keyed by field.
- Business-rule violations: **409** with `message` and a stable machine-readable `error` code (`order_not_payable`, `order_already_paid`, `order_has_payments`, `order_locked`, `invalid_status_transition`).
- **401** missing/invalid/expired token, **404** unknown resource *or one owned by another user*, **429** rate limit (60/min per user; 10/min per IP on login/register/refresh).

Every example response in this collection was recorded from the running API.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Register, log in, and manage the JWT. Every other endpoint needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; **Login** and **Register** store the token in the `token` collection variable automatically.

request.description:
Create an account and receive a JWT straight away.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `name` | required, string, max 255 |
| `email` | required, valid email, unique |
| `password` | required, min 8, must match `password_confirmation` |

Rate limited to 10 requests / minute per IP.

response.name: Registered (201)
Validation error (422)
Email already taken (422)

request.description:
Exchange email + password for a JWT. `expires_in` is in seconds (`JWT_TTL`, default 60 minutes).

The seeded demo account is `demo@example.com` / `password`.

Rate limited to 10 requests / minute per IP.

response.name: Logged in (200)
Wrong credentials (401)
Validation error (422)

request.description: Return the user the token belongs to.

response.name: Current user (200)
Missing or invalid token (401)
Token used after logout (401)

request.description: Exchange the current token for a new one. Works for an expired token as long as it is within `JWT_REFRESH_TTL` (default 2 weeks). The old token is blacklisted.

response.name: Refreshed (200)
Old or invalid token (401)

request.description: Invalidate (blacklist) the current token. Returns **204 No Content**.

item.name: Orders
item.description: Create, list, view, update and delete orders. Users only ever see their own orders; another user's order answers **404**.

request.description:
Paginated list of **your** orders, newest first.

| Query | Rules |
|---|---|
| `status` | optional: `pending`, `confirmed`, `cancelled` |
| `per_page` | optional, 1-100, default 15 |
| `page` | optional, default 1 |

The response carries Laravel's standard `links` and `meta` pagination blocks.

response.name: Filtered by status (200)
Paginated (200)
Invalid filter (422)

request.description:
Create an order. The server calculates each `line_total` and the order `total` (in integer cents, so no float rounding); any `status` or `total` sent by the client is ignored. New orders are always `pending`.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `customer.name` | required, max 255 |
| `customer.email` | required, valid email |
| `customer.phone` | optional, max 30 |
| `customer.address` | optional, max 500 |
| `items` | required, 1-100 items |
| `items.*.product_name` | required, max 255 |
| `items.*.quantity` | required, integer 1-10000 |
| `items.*.price` | required, 0.01-999999.99, max 2 decimals |
| `notes` | optional, max 1000 |

response.name: Created (201)
Validation error (422)

request.description: One order with its items and `payments_count`.

response.name: Order (200)
Not found (404)

request.description:
Partial update (`PUT` behaves the same). Send any of `customer` (any subset of its fields), `items` (replaces **all** items and recalculates the total), `notes`, `status`.

**Status transitions:** `pending -> confirmed | cancelled`, `confirmed -> cancelled`. `cancelled` is final.

**409 Conflict when:**
- the order is cancelled (no further changes),
- `items` is sent and the order already has any payment,
- `status` changes while a successful or pending payment exists,
- the transition is not allowed (`invalid_status_transition`).

response.name: Replace items, total recalculated (200)
Confirm order (200)
Invalid status transition (409)
Empty body (422)
Unknown status (422)
Cancelled order is final (409)
Paid order status locked (409)
Items locked after payment (409)

request.description: Delete an order and its items. Returns **204**. Orders with **any** associated payment (even failed) cannot be deleted: **409** `order_has_payments`. The database foreign key enforces the same rule.

response.name: Has payments (409)
Not found (404)

item.name: Payments
item.description: Process payments through a pluggable gateway (strategy pattern) and read payment history. Payments can only be processed for **confirmed** orders.

request.description: The values accepted as `payment_method`, read from the gateway registry (`config/payments.php`). A gateway added there appears here with no other change.

response.name: Available methods (200)

request.description:
Charge an order through the gateway registered for `payment_method`. The amount is always the order total; the client cannot set it.

`payment_details` is validated by **the selected gateway's own rules**, so each gateway brings its own fields:

**credit_card**: `card_number` (12-19 digits, Luhn-valid), `card_holder`, `expiry_month` (1-12), `expiry_year` (4 digits), `cvv` (3-4 digits). Only brand, last 4 digits and holder name are stored.

**paypal**: `paypal_email`.

**Simulated outcomes**

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| card `4242424242424242` (or any other valid number) | `successful` |
| card `4000000000000002` | `failed`, `card_declined` |
| card `4000000000009995` | `failed`, `insufficient_funds` |
| expiry in the past | `failed`, `expired_card` |
| PayPal email starting with `declined` | `failed`, `payer_declined` |

A processed attempt always returns **201** (the payment is recorded either way); read `data.status`. A failed payment can be retried; a successful or pending one blocks further attempts (**409** `order_already_paid`). Only **confirmed** orders can be paid (**409** `order_not_payable`).

response.name: Order not confirmed (409)
Gateway validation error (422)
Unsupported method (422)
Card declined, recorded as failed (201)
Credit card, successful (201)
Already paid (409)
PayPal, successful (201)

request.description: Paginated payments of one order, newest first. Optional filters: `status` (`pending`, `successful`, `failed`), `method`, `per_page`, `page`.

response.name: Payments of order (200)

request.description:
Paginated payments across all of **your** orders, newest first.

| Query | Rules |
|---|---|
| `status` | optional: `pending`, `successful`, `failed` |
| `method` | optional, e.g. `credit_card` |
| `order_id` | optional, integer |
| `per_page` | optional, 1-100, default 15 |
| `page` | optional |
